patient.chief_complaint: Two years of progressive bilateral foot numbness and burning, normal nerve tests
patient.history_present_illness: Denise Harrington is a 48-year-old high school teacher presenting for a second neurological opinion after 2 years of progressively worsening bilateral foot and lower leg numbness and burning pain that is worse at night. She has been evaluated by two prior neurologists and a podiatrist, and has had three normal EMG/NCS studies, leading to frustration and the suggestion that her symptoms are 'anxiety-related.' She categorically denies anxiety as the explanation and presents with a self-documented 2-year symptom diary. The pain wakes her from sleep nightly and prevents her from wearing shoes for more than 2 hours. She has had complete lab work twice (HbA1c 5.6% — prediabetic range, B12 normal, TSH normal) which was attributed to mild prediabetes. She reports that the numbness began in the plantar surface of both feet and has crept up both legs, reaching mid-calf. Temperature sensation is markedly reduced (she scalds her feet in hot baths without noticing). Notably, she has normal balance and does not drop things — motor and large fiber function appear intact clinically. She recently read about 'small fiber neuropathy' online and has brought printouts asking about skin biopsy. She has no diabetes on fasting glucose, no alcohol, no relevant toxic exposures, and no family history of neuropathy. She has had dry eyes for 6 years treated with cyclosporine drops. She had a miscarriage 4 years ago attributed to 'unknown causes.' She takes no medications beyond cyclosporine ophthalmic.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Small-fiber neuropathy with Sjögren's syndrome and antiphospholipid antibody overlap

differential.key_features: Diagnosis of exclusion; requires comprehensive workup for autoimmune, metabolic, hereditary, and paraneoplastic causes.
Anti-Hu / CV2 ganglionopathy can present subacutely; warrants malignancy screen.
Prediabetes (HbA1c 5.6%) can cause SFN; OGTT and HbA1c monitoring useful.
Younger onset typical; genetic panel if other causes negative.
Should not be diagnosis of exclusion without IENFD; here objective sensory loss to temperature argues for organic neuropathy.

optimal_actions.action: Order broad neuropathy labs (CBC, CMP, HbA1c, B12 + MMA, TSH, SPEP/IFE, urinalysis)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.action: Order EMG/NCS to characterize axonal vs demyelinating pattern and distribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.action: Search literature for DSP evaluation guidelines and etiology-specific recommendations
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm AAN 2009 DSP workup, etiology-specific evaluations

optimal_actions.action: Review medications for neurotoxic agents and check interactions for symptomatic therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify potentially neurotoxic drugs (chemotherapy, metronidazole, megadose B6, nitrofurantoin); guide neuropathic-pain pharmacotherapy

optimal_actions.action: Skin biopsy for intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IENFD below 97.5% lower limit for age/sex confirms small-fiber neuropathy

optimal_actions.action: Autonomic function testing (QSART, deep-breathing HRV, Valsalva)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sudomotor and/or cardiovagal dysfunction supports small-fiber / autonomic involvement

optimal_actions.action: Sjögren's and antiphospholipid serologies (anti-SSA, anti-SSB, lupus anticoagulant, anti-cardiolipin, anti-β2GP1) + paraneoplastic panel
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anti-SSA/SSB and persistent antiphospholipid antibodies (≥12 weeks apart) support overlap

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Advanced cerebral imaging (PET/MRA/MRV/perfusion) has no routine role in peripheral neuropathy.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.

critical_actions: Recognize the small-fiber phenotype (burning pain, temperature loss, allodynia) with intact large-fiber exam and normal EMG/NCS
Skin biopsy for IENFD is gold standard [Lauria_2010]
Autonomic testing (QSART, HRV) for autonomic involvement
Workup Sjögren's, antiphospholipid syndrome, and paraneoplastic causes given dry eyes / miscarriage / aphthous ulcers
contraindicated_actions: Do not dismiss as anxiety or functional — three normal EMG/NCS studies do not exclude small-fiber neuropathy
Do not start IVIG/steroids without etiologic confirmation and severity-disability documentation
key_reasoning_points: Normal EMG/NCS does NOT exclude small-fiber neuropathy — need IENFD
Dry eyes (6 years), recurrent aphthous ulcers, and a miscarriage point toward Sjögren's and/or antiphospholipid overlap
Three prior normal EMG/NCS are the leak — the diagnostic puzzle is to recognize that they are not the right test

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: EMG/NCS measures large fibers only; normal EMG/NCS does not exclude small-fiber neuropathy.
Objective temperature sensation loss, allodynia, and chronic dry eyes argue for organic small-fiber neuropathy with possible autoimmune overlap.
Prediabetes can contribute but does not explain coincident sicca and pregnancy loss; workup for autoimmune cause is required.
